description: Known-Answer Test suite v1 for the WS-D proving lane (stage2/arx-d2, D-4). Four classes per finding 05 §2.D2 / acceptance-criteria.md AC-D.7: TRUE-known-formal (completeness), TRUE-known-informal (mathlib-ceiling honesty), FALSE-must-reject (soundness — any proven-* here is a red alarm), OPEN-must-abstain (calibration). Entries with a `formal.snippet` were validated against the live mathlib REPL (leanprover/lean4:v4.30.0-rc2, mathlib 5450b53e5ddc75d46418fabb605edbf36bd0beb6) on 2026-07-04; witness snippets under `counterexample.witness_lean` likewise. `control_eligible` entries are cheap enough to embed as per-run controls (AC-D.8). Loaded and validated by server/kat.py::load_kat_fixture.

entries.statement_nl: The square root of 2 is irrational.
There are infinitely many prime numbers.

formal.statement_lean: ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ p, n ≤ p ∧ p.Prime
formal.snippet: theorem kat_tf02 (n : ℕ) : ∃ p, n ≤ p ∧ p.Prime := Nat.exists_infinite_primes n

entries.statement_nl: Every finite integral domain is a field.

formal.statement_lean: def Fintype.fieldOfDomain (R) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [DecidableEq R] [Fintype R] : Field R

entries.notes: Statement-only at v1 (instance-shaped; the autoformalizer must produce its own theorem form).

entries.statement_nl: The sum of two even integers is even.

formal.statement_lean: ∀ a b : ℤ, Even a → Even b → Even (a + b)
formal.snippet: theorem kat_tf04 (a b : ℤ) (ha : Even a) (hb : Even b) : Even (a + b) := by obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := ha; obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := hb; exact ⟨x + y, by omega⟩

entries.statement_nl: One plus one equals two.
entries.provenance: kernel-only seed (runs without mathlib — base-Lean fallback case)

entries.statement_nl: There is no largest natural number.

formal.snippet: theorem kat_tf06 (n : Nat) : ∃ m, n < m := ⟨n + 1, Nat.lt_succ_self n⟩

entries.statement_nl: 97 is a prime number.
The composition of two injective functions is injective.

formal.statement_lean: Function.Injective g → Function.Injective f → Function.Injective (g ∘ f)

entries.statement_nl: Every group of prime order is cyclic.

formal.statement_lean: Nat.Card G = p → [Fact p.Prime] → IsCyclic G

entries.statement_nl: Cantor's theorem: no function from a set to its power set is surjective.

formal.statement_lean: ∀ f : α → Set α, ¬ Function.Surjective f

entries.statement_nl: 2 is a prime number.
Every natural number is either even or odd.

formal.statement_lean: ∀ n : ℕ, Even n ∨ Odd n

entries.statement_nl: Serre duality holds for coherent sheaves on a smooth projective variety over an algebraically closed field.
entries.provenance: Hartshorne III.7; mathlib has no sheaf-cohomology-at-scale machinery (finding 05 §2.E math.AG ceiling)

entries.statement_nl: Kodaira vanishing: for an ample line bundle L on a smooth complex projective variety X, H^i(X, K_X ⊗ L) = 0 for i > 0.

informal.source: Kodaira 1953; Lazarsfeld, Positivity in Algebraic Geometry I, 4.2

entries.statement_nl: Serre vanishing: for a coherent sheaf F on a projective scheme X with ample O(1), H^i(X, F(n)) = 0 for all i > 0 and all sufficiently large n.
entries.provenance: Hartshorne III.5.2; the Enriques-article vanishing workhorse (finding 03)

entries.statement_nl: The Riemann-Roch theorem for a smooth projective curve: χ(D) = deg D + 1 − g.
A smooth projective curve of genus at least 2 over ℂ has a finite automorphism group (Hurwitz: |Aut| ≤ 84(g−1)).
Hodge decomposition: for a compact Kähler manifold X, H^k(X, ℂ) decomposes as the direct sum of H^{p,q}(X) with p + q = k.
entries.provenance: Voisin, Hodge Theory and Complex Algebraic Geometry I, 6.1

entries.statement_nl: The canonical bundle of a K3 surface is trivial.
entries.provenance: Huybrechts, Lectures on K3 Surfaces, Ch. 1 (bridgeland-stability notebook domain)

informal.source: Huybrechts, Lectures on K3 Surfaces, Ch. 1

entries.statement_nl: An Enriques surface has 2-torsion canonical bundle: K_X is not trivial but K_X ⊗ K_X ≅ O_X.
entries.provenance: Enriques/Kuznetsov article corpus (finding 03); Barth-Hulek-Peters-Van de Ven VIII

informal.source: Barth-Hulek-Peters-Van de Ven, Compact Complex Surfaces, VIII

entries.statement_nl: Bridgeland's deformation theorem: the space Stab(D) of stability conditions on a triangulated category D, with the natural topology, is a complex manifold and the central-charge map is a local homeomorphism.
entries.provenance: Bridgeland 2007 (Ann. Math. 166); textbook form in the ingested Huybrechts segments (bridgeland-stability-pdfs notebook)

informal.source: Bridgeland, Stability conditions on triangulated categories, Thm 1.2; Huybrechts segments in bridgeland-stability-pdfs

entries.statement_nl: Every object of the bounded derived category of coherent sheaves on P^1 is isomorphic to a finite direct sum of shifts of line bundles O(a).
entries.provenance: Beilinson/Grothendieck splitting; Huybrechts, Fourier-Mukai Transforms, 3.15 (fourier-duality notebook domain)

informal.source: Huybrechts, Fourier-Mukai Transforms in Algebraic Geometry, Cor. 3.15

entries.statement_nl: Every group of order 6 is abelian.

counterexample.description: S₃ (the symmetric group on 3 letters) has order 6 and is non-abelian: (0 1) and (1 2) do not commute.

witness_lean.snippet:
theorem kat_fm01_witness : ∃ a b : Equiv.Perm (Fin 3), a * b ≠ b * a := by
  refine ⟨Equiv.swap 0 1, Equiv.swap 1 2, ?_⟩
  decide

discharges.proposition: ∃ a b : Equiv.Perm (Fin 3), a * b ≠ b * a
discharges.justification: Two non-commuting elements of S₃ (order 6) witness a non-abelian group of order 6, refuting 'every group of order 6 is abelian'. NOTE (durable P1 kernel-decides): the proposition is written in NATURAL author syntax; verdict linkage no longer string-compares — THE KERNEL checks `example : <this> := @kat_fm01_witness`, which accepts any form definitionally equal to the witness's type (live-verified this LINKS).

entries.statement_nl: n² + n + 41 is prime for every natural number n.

discharges.justification: n = 40 makes 40²+40+41 = 1681 = 41² composite, a direct counterexample to the universal 'n²+n+41 is prime'. NAMED-declaration contract (durable P1): the former anonymous `example` had no kernel-queryable name, so it is now a NAMED theorem so `example : <proposition> := @kat_fm02_witness` is checkable. The proposition is written in NATURAL author syntax (kernel-decides accepts any defeq form).

entries.statement_nl: All Fermat numbers F_n = 2^(2^n) + 1 are prime.
entries.provenance: acceptance-criteria.md §WS-D seed (Fermat's conjecture, refuted by Euler 1732)

discharges.justification: F₅ = 2^32+1 factors as 641 × 6700417 (Euler), so F₅ is composite — refuting 'all Fermat numbers are prime'. The witness proves the auxiliary factorization the kernel can check; the entailment to ¬claim is the recorded, attested obligation.

entries.statement_nl: The sum of two irrational numbers is irrational.

counterexample.description: √2 + (−√2) = 0, which is rational; both summands are irrational.

witness_lean.snippet:
theorem kat_fm04_witness : ¬ Irrational (Real.sqrt 2 + -(Real.sqrt 2)) := by
  rw [add_neg_cancel]
  exact not_irrational_zero

discharges.justification: √2 and −√2 are both irrational but sum to 0 (rational), refuting 'the sum of two irrationals is irrational'. NOTE (durable P1 kernel-decides): written in NATURAL author syntax (`Real.sqrt`, space after ¬); THE KERNEL checks `example : <this> := @kat_fm04_witness` and accepts any defeq form (`Real.sqrt`↔`√` — live-verified this LINKS).

entries.statement_nl: Every continuous real-valued function on the open interval (0,1) attains its maximum.
entries.provenance: acceptance-criteria.md §WS-D seed — hypothesis-dropped mutation of the true extreme-value theorem on [0,1] (compactness removed)

counterexample.description: f(x) = x is continuous on (0,1) with supremum 1, attained by no point of (0,1). (Also f(x) = 1/x is continuous and unbounded.)

entries.notes: The L1 gate should also catch this shape when an autoformalizer silently strengthens (0,1) to [0,1] — the Erdős-misformalization taxonomy 'missing hypothesis' case.

entries.statement_nl: Euler's sum-of-powers conjecture for k = 5: no four positive fifth powers sum to a fifth power.

discharges.justification: Lander-Parkin (1966): four positive fifth powers summing to a fifth power, refuting Euler's k=5 sum-of-powers conjecture. The witness proves the auxiliary identity; the entailment to ¬claim is the attested obligation.

entries.statement_nl: Pólya's conjecture: for every N > 1, at least half of the naturals up to N have an odd number of prime factors (counted with multiplicity).
entries.provenance: acceptance-criteria.md §WS-D seed — the large-counterexample humility case

counterexample.description: First counterexample N = 906,150,257 (Tanaka 1980; conjecture disproved by Haselgrove 1958). Far beyond slim_check/decide reach — the pipeline must refute via L4 literature or abstain, never 'support' it from numeric sweeps at small N.

entries.statement_nl: Mertens conjecture: |M(n)| ≤ √n for all n > 1, where M is the Mertens function.

counterexample.description: Disproved by Odlyzko-te Riele (1985) without an explicit counterexample; the first violation is known only to lie below exp(1.59×10^40). Must resolve via L4-verified citation or abstain — never 'prove', and never 'refute' with a fabricated witness.

entries.statement_nl: The sum of two odd integers is odd.
entries.provenance: parity mutation of kat-tf-04 (Erdős-misformalization taxonomy: strength/parity flip)

discharges.justification: 1 and 1 are both odd but 1+1 = 2 is even, refuting 'the sum of two odd integers is odd'. NOTE (durable P1 kernel-decides): written in NATURAL author syntax with the explicit `(1 : ℤ)` ascription; THE KERNEL checks `example : <this> := @kat_fm09_witness` and accepts any defeq form (the ascription elides once elaborated — live-verified this LINKS).

entries.statement_nl: There is a largest prime number.
entries.provenance: negation mutation of kat-tf-02 (∀/∃ swap class)

counterexample.description: Euclid: for any prime p there is a prime above p + 1. Refutable by a direct Lean proof of the negation — the refuted lane's proof-of-negation case, not just a numeric witness.

witness_lean.snippet:
theorem kat_fm10_witness : ¬ ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ ∀ q : ℕ, q.Prime → q ≤ p := by
  rintro ⟨p, hp, hmax⟩
  obtain ⟨q, hle, hq⟩ := Nat.exists_infinite_primes (p + 1)
  exact absurd (hmax q hq) (by omega)

discharges.proposition: ¬ ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ ∀ q : ℕ, q.Prime → q ≤ p
discharges.justification: A direct Lean proof of the negation of 'there is a largest prime' (Euclid): no prime bounds all primes. NOTE (durable P1 kernel-decides): written in NATURAL author syntax (`p.Prime`, explicit binder types, space after ¬); THE KERNEL checks `example : <this> := @kat_fm10_witness` and accepts any defeq form (`p.Prime`↔`Nat.Prime p` — live-verified this LINKS).

entries.statement_nl: Every prime number is odd.
entries.provenance: hypothesis-dropped mutation ('odd prime' → 'prime'); classic edge-case miss

witness_lean.snippet:
theorem kat_fm11_witness : ¬ (∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → Odd p) := fun h =>
  absurd (h 2 Nat.prime_two) (by decide)

discharges.justification: 2 is prime and even, refuting 'every prime is odd' (the dropped 'odd prime' → 'prime' hypothesis). NOTE (durable P1 kernel-decides): written in NATURAL author syntax (`p.Prime`, outer parens, space after ¬); THE KERNEL checks `example : <this> := @kat_fm11_witness` and accepts any defeq form (live-verified this LINKS).

entries.statement_nl: For every prime p, the Mersenne number 2^p − 1 is prime.

discharges.justification: p = 11 (prime) gives 2^11−1 = 2047 = 23 × 89 composite, refuting 'for every prime p, 2^p−1 is prime'. The witness proves the auxiliary factorization; the entailment to ¬claim is the attested obligation.

entries.statement_nl: Goldbach conjecture: every even integer greater than 2 is the sum of two primes.
entries.provenance: acceptance-criteria.md §WS-D seed; formalized in DeepMind formal-conjectures

entries.statement_nl: Twin prime conjecture: there are infinitely many primes p with p + 2 prime.
entries.provenance: acceptance-criteria.md §WS-D seed; formalized in DeepMind formal-conjectures

entries.statement_nl: The Euler-Mascheroni constant γ is irrational.
entries.provenance: acceptance-criteria.md §WS-D seed (open; not even known transcendental)

entries.statement_nl: Collatz conjecture: iterating n → n/2 (n even), n → 3n+1 (n odd) reaches 1 from every positive integer.
Riemann Hypothesis: all non-trivial zeros of ζ(s) have real part 1/2.
entries.provenance: DeepMind formal-conjectures (Lean-formalized statement); mathlib has RiemannHypothesis as a def

entries.statement_nl: Legendre's conjecture: there is a prime between n² and (n+1)² for every positive integer n.
No odd perfect number exists.
entries.provenance: DeepMind formal-conjectures class (ancient open problem; checked beyond 10^1500)
entries.notes: Numeric sweeps supporting nonexistence are exactly the 'statistical evidence masquerading as proof' trap (finding 05 §2.C escape 5).

entries.statement_nl: Erdős-Straus conjecture: for every n ≥ 2, 4/n = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z has a solution in positive integers.
Brocard's problem: n! + 1 = m² has no solution with n > 7.
There are infinitely many Mersenne primes.
entries.provenance: open (pairs with kat-fm-12: the FALSE 'all Mersenne numbers with prime exponent are prime' vs the OPEN infinitude)
